name: Beresheet
first: First privately-funded mission to reach the Moon; first Israeli lunar mission
description: SpaceIL's Beresheet (Hebrew: 'In the beginning') launched as a shared-ride passenger on a Falcon 9 in February 2019. Instead of a direct trans-lunar injection, the small lander performed weeks of perigee-raising phasing burns to climb from a parking orbit out to the Moon — a fuel-saving trajectory pioneered for low-budget missions. After successful lunar orbit insertion on 4 April 2019, an inertial measurement unit reset during descent caused the main engine to shut down. Beresheet crashed in Mare Serenitatis. SpaceIL committed to a successor (Beresheet 2) within days.

events.label: PHASING BURN
events.note: First of seven perigee raises to climb from LEO to lunar approach.

events.label: TCM 2
events.note: Second TCM. Apogee approaching lunar capture distance.

events.label: LUNAR APPROACH
events.note: Final translunar burn — Beresheet on direct lunar trajectory.

events.label: DESCENT ANOMALY
events.note: IMU reset during powered descent → engine shutdown → crash in Mare Serenitatis 2019-04-11.
